## New cap table + memory math (`/home/siah/creative/reactjit/world_loader.zig:76-91`)

| Family | Old | New | GPU bytes/row | GPU total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| grass | 65536 | 262144 | 24 (SlimInstance) | 6.3 MB |
| bush | 16384 | 65536 | 24 | 1.6 MB |
| flower | 16384 | 65536 | 24 | 1.6 MB |
| frond | 24576 | 262144 | 24 | 6.3 MB |
| trunk | 2048 | 16384 | 80 (InstanceData) | 1.3 MB |

Frond:trunk held at exactly 16:1 (262144/16384) matching one palm = 1 trunk + ~16 crown fronds — the old ratio was 12:1, which is why fronds exhausted at ~1.5k palms while trunks kept placing. CPU side: 12 f32/row → ~31 MB across all five buffers, allocated lazily once (`ensureFoliageBuf` allocates cap-sized exactly once per family; verified the cap constant is the same one passed at all call sites).

## Saturation visibility

Per-family flags (`grass_full` … `trunk_full`) replace the single `full` bool; the one-per-regen log line now appends ` CLIPPED` after whichever family's count/cap hit the wall, via a named `clippedMark` helper. Message text otherwise preserved for the next UI slice to parse.

- `SHIP_RUN_PACKAGE=0 ./tools/rjit ship editor` → queued behind another build, then: `[ship] done (packaging skipped) -> /home/siah/creative/reactjit/zig-out/bin/editor` — compiled clean.
- Visual proof is NOT claimed — that happens in the user's live critique round (painting a forest and confirming crowned palms).

## GPU-side findings (3d.zig read-only, not edited)

- No hard clip for these caps. Each family batch (max 262,144 rows) fits `MAX_STATIC_INSTANCES = 1048576` (`framework/gpu/3d.zig:3868`), and retention refusal falls back to the per-frame dynamic path (`static_instance_policy.zig:7`, fallback at `3d.zig:6689`) — degraded, not dropped.
- One pressure point to flag, not a bug: retention is whole-array = the cap-sized slice (`3d.zig:5749`, world_loader passes `buf` not `buf[0..n]` by design for stable offsets), so the paint preview now reserves up to 655,360 of the 1,048,576-row shared slim pool once all four slim families first upload — 62.5%, leaving ~393k rows for the baked world's own slim foliage batches before latecomers drop to the per-frame path (`3d.zig:3934` documents that overflow mode). Fine today; if slim-pool contention shows up later, `MAX_STATIC_INSTANCES` is the lever (owned by the other agent's file).
